pnl_definition: PnL is Net Trading Income (NTI), the line Optiver uses in its consolidated Optiver Holding B.V. annual reports and reviews. It is trading results net of direct trading costs (exchange, clearing and financing-type costs), BEFORE personnel and other operating expenses. Figures are calendar-year and reported in EUR, converted to USD at the annual-average EURUSD rate. It is NOT gross trading income. The statutory accounts carry a gross 'trading income' / 'bruto handelswinst' line about 30% higher (2014: 804.7 vs NTI 619.8; 2015: ~1,206 vs ~930; 2024: >4,500 vs 3,494), which Dutch press sometimes quotes as 'omzet'. Net profit attributable to equity holders is recorded separately in net_income_usd_m.
headcount_definition: Group-wide employees of Optiver Holding B.V. across all offices: Amsterdam, Chicago, Austin, Sydney, Hong Kong, Shanghai, Singapore, Taipei, London, plus New York from 2025. The count is Optiver's reported year-end full-time employees / FTE. The 2019 and 2020 reviews explicitly say 'at end-2019' and 'at the end of 2020'. The 2023-2025 reviews say 'Total full-time employees', which is presumed year-end and forms a continuous series with the 2022 FTE figure. Interns (e.g. 299 in 2024), Academy trainees and contractors appear to be excluded. For 2015-2017 the basis (FTE vs heads, year-end vs average) is unclear. The 2026 value is an estimated mid-2026 level. Because these are year-end figures, NTI per year-end head understates NTI per average head in fast-growth years (about 6-11% in 2021-2023).
fx_note: EUR to USD at annual-average rates (USD per EUR): 2015 1.110, 2016 1.107, 2017 1.130, 2018 1.181, 2019 1.120, 2020 1.142, 2021 1.183, 2022 1.053, 2023 1.081, 2024 1.082, 2025 ~1.13. The 2025 rate is approximate; my recollection of the ECB 2025 average is ~1.129, which I could not re-verify in this run. The 2026 YTD rate is ~1.16 (approximate, used only to express the USD-based H1-2026 estimate in EUR). The 2026 estimate was built in USD. H1-2025 Optiver NTI was converted at ~1.093, my approximate average of the ECB monthly rates for Jan-Jun 2025, which I did not verify. Much of Optiver's NTI is earned in USD (US options), so EURUSD moves distort reported EUR growth. FY2025 NTI grew +30% in EUR but ~+36% in USD. The 2025 USD bars include about ±1% extra for FX-rate uncertainty. Regional figures in AUD (Optiver Australia) and GBP (Optiver UK Ltd) are context only and are not converted into the group rows.
methodology: Four research lenses (press, primary, headcount, recent) were merged into one series of Optiver Holding B.V. group Net Trading Income and year-end FTE. Optiver's own annual reviews and results releases were preferred: the 2019-2025 PDFs were downloaded and read, and prior-year comparatives cross-check each other. Quote (quotenet.nl) articles reading the KvK-filed accounts fill 2015-2018. The series was chain-checked through reported percentage changes: 813 → +60% → ~1,301; official 2019 1,133 = -13% vs 2018 → ~1,302; 2020 ~3.19bn → -28% → ~2.30bn → +42% → 3,290. Rounded or derived years were bracketed by the rounding limits of those percentages. For 2015 the gross-vs-net trap was resolved by reconciliation. Quote's EUR1,206m 'handelsomzet' is gross trading income. NTI of ~EUR930m follows from three consistent figures: the 2014 NTI of 619.8 × 1.50, the Scribd summary figure of 929.7, and the cost structure (operating result ~502 + personnel ≥338 + other opex ~90). Optiver publishes no interim results. The 2026 row is therefore a model estimate for 2026-01-01 to 2026-06-30. It takes half of FY2025 NTI and scales it by a peer-regime factor. That factor comes from Virtu Financial's Q2-2026 10-Q: Market Making Adjusted Net Trading Income +46% YoY in H1 2026. This is outside the Optiver evidence set and was read from the project's shared data. It was dampened by Optiver's historical beta of ~0.65-0.9 to Virtu market-making growth (2024 USD +26% vs Virtu MM +41%; 2025 USD +36% vs +39%).

entities.name: Optiver (group-wide)
entities.description: Optiver Holding B.V. consolidated group (Amsterdam HQ; US/Chicago-Austin-New York, APAC/Sydney-Hong Kong-Shanghai-Singapore-Taipei, London). It excludes standalone regional-entity figures such as Optiver Australia Pty Ltd, Optiver UK Ltd and Optiver US LLC, which are not additive. Northpool (majority stake announced 2026-08-18, completion expected Nov 2026) is not included.

rows.notes: NTI is ~EUR930m (range EUR885-1,040m) at 1.110. Quote and Amsterdamtrader report EUR1,206m 'handelsomzet' / 'trading result', but this is GROSS trading income. It is +50% on the 2014 gross line of 804.7, and the gross/net ratio of ~0.77 matches 2014 and 2024. The NTI of 929.7 comes from a Scribd summary (search snippet only, unverified). It equals the official 2014 NTI of 619.8 × 1.50 exactly and reconciles with the operating result of ~EUR502m, personnel costs of ≥EUR338m (EUR370k × 913) and other opex of ~EUR90m. Treating 1,206 as NTI would imply other opex of ~EUR366m, against ~110-135 in 2016-18. The upper bar still allows some chance of a definitional difference. Net profit attributable is EUR394.8m (Quote, from the KvK filing, matching the official 2014 comparative). Headcount 913: Quote calls it 'gemiddeld' (average), while Amsterdamtrader and Wikipedia (citing a dead Optiver press release) treat it as the year count. An average of 913 would imply a year-end of ~1,019, above 2016's 997, so it is more likely year-end. Basis unclear; bars ±5%.

No direct 2016 figure was found. NTI of ~EUR856m (range EUR830-885m) at 1.107 is back-calculated from Quote's FY2017 article: EUR813m was 'down 5%', and rounding the 5% alone gives EUR851-861m. The bars are widened for method risk. Net profit of ~EUR321m is derived from 2017's EUR279m (-13%). An FD headline (paywalled, not read) confirms that 2016 profit fell. A year of lower volatility after the 2015 boom is consistent with a decline. Headcount 997 is the Wikipedia infobox citing the Optiver 2016 Annual Review (dead S3 link, unverified). It is independently consistent with Quote's 2017 '1,020 FTE, +23'. FTE vs heads is unknown.

NTI is EUR813m (-5%) at 1.130, from Quote reading the KvK-filed 2017 accounts. Quote calls it 'omzet' / 'nettohandelsinkomsten'; it is the low-volatility year. It is chain-validated: Quote's 2018 +60% gives EUR1,301m, matching the ~EUR1,302m implied by Optiver's own 2019 release (-13%). Bars are ±3% for a single press outlet. Net profit is EUR279m and personnel costs EUR306m. Headcount is 1,020 FTE ('toename van 23'). Year-end vs average is not stated; it is likely year-end.

NTI is ~EUR1,300m (range EUR1,280-1,320m) at 1.181. Quote, from the KvK filing, gives 'nettohandelsresultaat +60% to EUR1.3bn' (813 × 1.6 = 1,301). Optiver's 2019 release ('2019 NTI EUR1,133m, 13% less than 2018') implies ~EUR1,302m, and Quote's -12.6% implies ~EUR1,296m. Net profit is EUR515m (official comparative) and the operating result EUR673m. Headcount is 1,038 FTE at end-2018 per the official comparative in the 2019 Annual Review; Quote has the same number. Personnel costs were EUR506m.

Official NTI is EUR1,133m (-13%) at 1.120. Bars of ±2% reflect FX convention and the annual review being a summary of the statutory accounts. Net profit attributable is EUR397m, the operating result EUR525m, and the salary-plus-bonus pool EUR388m (Quote). Headcount is 1,108 FTE 'at end-2019' (Annual Review 2019). Wikipedia's 1,109 is a transcription variant. The upper bar allows for heads > FTE.

Official NTI is 'EUR3.2bn, 180% more than 2019', rounded to EUR0.1bn. Quote (KvK filing) says 'bijna EUR3,2 miljard'. 1,133 × 2.8 = 3,172, and the 2021 figure of EUR2.3bn at -28% implies ~3,190-3,210. Point estimate EUR3,185m, range EUR3,120-3,240m, at 1.142. This was the COVID-volatility boom year. Net profit is EUR1,376m (Quote, from the KvK filing; Optiver rounds to EUR1.4bn). Personnel costs were EUR1,158m (~EUR965k per head). Headcount is '1,200 FTEs at the end of 2020' per the Annual Review 2020; the figure is rounded, and the Apr-2021 boilerplate says 'nearly 1,200'.

Official NTI is 'EUR2.3bn, 28% lower than 2020', rounded to EUR0.1bn. 2022's EUR3,290m at +42% implies ~EUR2,317m, and 2020's ~3,185 at -28% implies ~2,293. Point estimate EUR2,310m, range EUR2,255-2,350m, at 1.183. This was the retail/crypto boom year, but Optiver was down from the 2020 peak. Net profit attributable is EUR958m and the operating result ~EUR1.2bn. Headcount is 1,390 total FTEs (2021 comparative in the Annual Review 2022). The 2021 Annual Review PDF itself is now 404.

Official NTI is EUR3,290m (exact comparative in the Annual Review 2023; the AR2022 says 'EUR3.3bn, +42%') at 1.053. The weak euro boosts USD less than EUR. Bars are ±2%. Net profit attributable is EUR1,286m and the operating result EUR1,636m; implied total opex is ~EUR1,654m. Total assets jumped to EUR61.6bn as the US business grew. Headcount is 1,709 FTEs (+319), stated in AR2022 and repeated as the AR2023 comparative.

Official NTI is EUR2,773m (-16%) at 1.081, from the Annual Review 2023 and the press release, matched by the AR2024 comparative. Net profit attributable is EUR1,158m and the operating result EUR1,311m. Headcount is 1,952 'total full-time employees' (also the AR2024 comparative). 319 interns are listed separately and excluded. Optiver Australia (a regional entity) reported A$735m revenue and a loss in 2023 (Capital Brief); this is context only and not additive.

Official NTI is EUR3,494m (+26%) at 1.082. Quote's 'bruto handelswinst ruim EUR4,5 miljard' for 2024 is GROSS trading income before direct trading costs; do not use it. Wikipedia's 'Revenue EUR3.5bn' is in fact NTI. Net profit attributable is EUR1,369m and the operating result EUR1,777m. Headcount is 2,112 total full-time employees (the boilerplate says '2,100' and 'more than 2,000'), with 299 interns and 192 Academy trainees excluded. Regional context, not additive: Optiver Australia had A$1.2bn revenue and A$138m profit with about 500 Sydney staff.

Official NTI is EUR4,556m (+30% in EUR, ~+36% in USD) at ~1.13; the bars include about ±1% for FX-rate uncertainty. Source: the Annual Report 2025 and the 2026-03-31 release. The '€0.556B' on the scraped results page is a widget glitch. Net profit attributable is EUR1,769m, the operating result EUR2,336m, and equity EUR5,490m. Headcount is 2,233 'full-time employees' from the release key figures. Low-reliability conflicting figures are ignored: Substack 2,707 (unsourced) and Built In 1,600 (AI-generated, stale). Context points: APAC had about 800 staff (Oct 2025), and the UK service entity had 148 average / 152 year-end FTE, showing year-end runs ~3% above average.

rows.period_label: 2026-01-01 to 2026-06-30 (H1 2026, model estimate; no Optiver 2026 PnL has been published)
rows.notes: Optiver reports annually only (FY2026 expected ~late March 2027), so this is a MODEL ESTIMATE, not data. Method: H1-2025 NTI ≈ 50% of FY2025 (±5pp) → ~EUR2,278m ≈ $2.49bn at ~1.093. This is scaled by +33% USD growth (90% range ~+5% to +60%). The growth assumption comes from Virtu Financial's H1-2026 Market Making Adjusted Net Trading Income, +46% YoY per Virtu's Q2-2026 10-Q, a peer proxy outside the Optiver evidence. It is dampened by Optiver's historical ~0.65-0.9 beta to Virtu market-making growth. The supporting indicator is Optiver's 13F reported value: $371bn at 2026-06-30 vs $210bn a year earlier. That is mostly option notional, not PnL. The result is ~$3.3bn (≈EUR2.85bn at ~1.16), annualizing to ~$6.6bn (+28% vs 2025). Headcount is an estimated mid-2026 level: 2,233 at end-2025 plus ~3% half-year growth (the 2024-25 pace was +6-8% a year). The low bar is set by The Pragmatic Engineer's '~2,200' (Aug 2026, probably a rounded 2025 figure) and the 'over 2,000' boilerplate (2026-08-18). The high bar allows for faster hiring; the unsourced 2,707 (Substack) is not credited. Northpool (deal closing ~Nov 2026) is excluded.

ytd_2026.description: No reliable 2026 PnL exists for Optiver. Optiver Holding B.V. publishes consolidated results only once a year: FY2025 was released 2026-03-31, and FY2026 is expected around late March 2027. The latest REPORTED PnL therefore ends 2025-12-31. The 2026 row is a model estimate of H1 2026 NTI (cutoff 2026-06-30). That cutoff was chosen because it is the latest period with hard peer data: Virtu's Q2-2026 10-Q shows Market Making Adjusted Net Trading Income +46% YoY. Optiver's own Q2-2026 13F shows continued US book growth. The estimate is ~$3.3bn (90% CI $2.45-4.15bn). Headcount is an estimated ~2,300 mid-2026 (range 2,200-2,480). The latest Optiver-sourced indications are 'over 2,000 employees' (press release, 2026-08-18) and '~2,200' (The Pragmatic Engineer, 2026-08-11).

caveats: PnL is Optiver's own 'net trading income', which comes after direct trading costs such as exchange, clearing and financing. Optiver's statutory accounts also carry a GROSS trading income line about 30% higher. Dutch press sometimes quotes the gross line as 'omzet' or 'bruto handelswinst': 2015 EUR1,206m vs NTI ~930; 2024 '>EUR4.5bn' vs NTI 3,494. Peer comparisons must use like-for-like net definitions.

2019-2025 come from Optiver's annual reviews and press releases, which summarise the audited KvK-filed accounts; the full statutory jaarrekening was not read. The exact NTI construction (interest/financing, rebates, FX on trading positions) was not verified line by line.

2015 NTI is derived. The ~EUR930m rests on reconciliation and an unverified Scribd snippet, not a fetched primary document. 2016 NTI, net profit and headcount are back-calculated from percentage changes or come from Wikipedia citing dead primary links.
2020 and 2021 official NTI are rounded to EUR0.1bn (3.2bn and 2.3bn); point estimates come from cross-year percentage changes.

Everything is reported in EUR. A large share of NTI is earned in USD, so reported EUR growth understates USD growth when the euro strengthens (2025) and overstates it when the euro weakens (2022). The 2025 and 2026 FX rates are approximate.

Headcount is year-end FTE ('total full-time employees'), excluding interns (299 in 2024), Academy trainees and contractors. Physical heads may run a few percent above FTE. Dividing annual NTI by year-end FTE understates per-average-head productivity in growth years: averages of adjacent year-ends are 1,295 / 1,550 / 1,831 / 2,032 / 2,173 for 2021-2025. 2015-2017 headcount bases (FTE vs heads, average vs year-end) are unclear.

2026 is a MODEL ESTIMATE of H1 2026 (cutoff 2026-06-30), not reported data; Optiver publishes no interim results. It relies on a peer proxy (Virtu H1-2026 market-making growth of +46%, from Virtu's 10-Q, outside the Optiver evidence set) and an assumed 50/50 H1/H2 seasonality. Do not compare it directly with full-year figures without annualising.
From about Nov 2026 the Northpool majority stake (European power and gas trading) will change the consolidation scope and the per-head mix. It is excluded here.
Regional entity figures (Optiver Australia A$1.2bn revenue in 2024; Optiver UK Ltd cost-plus income) include intercompany or transfer-pricing effects and are not additive to the group.

Search budget note: the shared web-search budget was exhausted during this run. Bloomberg, FT, FD and AFR cross-checks were not possible, and pre-2019 figures depend mainly on one outlet (Quote) reading KvK filings, though they are internally chain-consistent with Optiver's own releases.
